metadata.title: Results from TALIS Starting Strong 2024: Chile

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD TALIS Starting Strong 2024 note reports descriptive survey results from questionnaires administered to ECEC staff and setting leaders in participating countries and subnational entities. The document does not specify the exact sampling weights or replicate-weight scheme used in the underlying TALIS Starting Strong 2024 database, nor does it name any weight variables. For analysts using the TALIS Starting Strong 2024 microdata, the appropriate approach is to apply the survey design weights provided with the database to obtain population-representative estimates within each participating entity and ECEC level (ISCED 02; and under-3 settings where applicable). Because this note is not an ML predictive analysis, plausible values and missing-data imputation strategies are not part of the reported methodology; however, standard complex-survey variance estimation should be used when computing uncertainty around percentages.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable because this note is based on questionnaire self-reports and reports indicator percentages (e.g., shares of staff/leaders/settings agreeing with statements or reporting activities), rather than cognitive achievement scores that would be PV-based. Missing-data handling is not reported because the note is a participant-country results note summarizing indicator outputs from the TALIS Starting Strong 2024 database, without detailing the microdata cleaning/imputation pipeline.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The note describes that TALIS Starting Strong 2024 aims to obtain a representative sample of staff and leaders in each participating country/subnational entity for each ECEC level covered. In Chile, it includes public, private and co-financed nurseries and kindergartens (sala cuna y jardín infantil) at the middle level (nivel medio) serving children age 2-4, and public, private and co-financed early childhood schools and kindergartens (escuelas y jardines infantiles) for transition levels 1 and 2 (pre-kinder y kinder) serving children age 4-6. The document does not provide the exact analytic-sample inclusion/exclusion rules (e.g., response-rate thresholds, item nonresponse handling, or any specific filtering beyond the ECEC level definitions).

data.outcome_summary: TALIS Starting Strong 2024 is an OECD large-scale survey of ECEC staff and setting leaders, using questionnaires to capture staff/leader demographics, training and daily work, practices with children and families, and well-being, job satisfaction, and career intentions. This Chile participant note summarizes indicator percentages for ISCED 02 pre-primary settings (and describes additional under-3 coverage in the broader survey), based exclusively on self-reports. The note highlights high family engagement in Chile (93% of staff encourage play/learning at home; 48% of leaders offer parent workshops several times a year) and high participation in job-embedded training and collaborative learning (72% of staff). It also reports lower staff stress than in other entities (36% report stress), with special education needs as a key stress source, and strong leader practices such as feedback and support for staff collaboration (53% and 49%, respectively). The document cautions that estimates should be interpreted with higher risk of non-response bias, and it does not report ML model performance metrics because no predictive modeling is conducted in this note.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a descriptive results note from the TALIS Starting Strong 2024 database rather than an empirical ML/predictive study. As a result, there is no student-level analytic sample size, no PV-based achievement outcome, no missing-data/PV handling strategy, and no ML algorithms or performance metrics to extract. The extraction therefore focuses on the survey scope (ECEC levels and participating entities) and the reported indicator outcomes, while leaving ML-specific fields empty by design.
